overview_description: List and read the days of the month a date can be aligned to.
intro: The days of the month are the fixed set of days a date can be aligned to, each with a `day` number. You can list them and read one. This area has 2 endpoints, and all seven SDKs call every one.
notes: **This area is read only.** There are no create, update or delete calls.
**A day of the month `id` starts with `dom_`.** A single read returns the record under `day_of_month`.
**`day` holds the day number.** It is an integer.
**Listings page by cursor.** Records sit under `data`; pass `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` to read the next page, and stop when `pagination.has_more` is `false`.

endpoints.title: List days of the month
endpoints.summary: Returns a page of the days of the month a date can be aligned to, under `data`.
endpoints.description: Lists the days of the month a date can be aligned to. Each record carries its `day` number. Pass `limit` to set the page size, and while `pagination.has_more` is true pass `pagination.next_cursor` back as `cursor` to read the next page. Other fields filter as `filter_<field>` or `filter_<field>_<operator>`, and `sort` orders the results.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many records to return on one page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `pagination.next_cursor` of the previous page, to read the next one.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by. Prefix it with `-` for descending order, such as `-created_on`.

200.description: A page of days of the month, under `data`.

endpoints.title: Retrieve a day of the month
endpoints.summary: Returns one day of the month by its `dom_` `id`, under `day_of_month`.
endpoints.description: Reads the day of the month with this `dom_` `id`.

parameters.name: day_of_month_id
parameters.description: The day of the month's `dom_` `id`, as the listing returns it.

200.description: The day of the month, under `day_of_month`.

limit.description: The page size applied to this page.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows. Trust this over `next_cursor`, which can still be set on the last page.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as `cursor` to read the next page.
